title: Canonical grading and degree-zero residue isomorphism
statement: Let A be a commutative local ring. Its homogeneous subgroups tangentGrading A n [def-sfb-nodal-tangent-comparison-data] carry a canonical GradedRing structure. There is a canonical ring isomorphism A/m ≃ (tangentGrading A)₀ sending the class of a to its degree-zero initial class in the associated graded ring [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. No reducedness, finiteness or nodal hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Each direct-sum inclusion is injective. Identify each summand additively with its range. The direct sum of these equivalences has inverse the sum of subgroup inclusions: check this on every summand using DirectSum.addHom_ext and coeAddMonoidHom_of. Therefore the homogeneous subgroups form an internal direct sum.

proof.text: Use the internal direct sum to obtain the decomposition. The associated graded unit lies in degree zero and the product of inclusions is the inclusion of associatedGradedMul in the sum of degrees. These prove the GradedRing fields.

source.place: Tag 0CBT, omitted equivalence of constructions (2) and (3); Tags 0CBU and 0CBW for branches.

proof.text: The associatedGradedRingHom lands in the degree-zero subgroup and kills m. Factor through A/m. Injectivity follows from the proved associated-graded residue-algebra injection; surjectivity follows by lifting the degree-zero graded piece through its submodule quotient. The representative formula is definitional.
